Figure 1 — Clinical utility cascade

PDF vector · TIFF 600 dpi

Figure 1. Patient-level cascade; percentages use the full cohort denominator. Among 122 sampled POP cases, 81/122 (66.4%) had positive pre-extubation microbiology. Specific overlap was present in 33/81 (40.7%) positive samples. Specific overlap with inadequate empirical therapy was documented in 8/122 (6.6%) of the cohort. This is a candidate opportunity, not demonstrated preventability. Adequacy was missing in 2 specifically concordant cases.

Figure 2 — Resistance and empirical inadequacy

PDF vector · TIFF 600 dpi

Figure 2. Proportion of inadequate empirical therapy by recorded resistance status, with exact binomial 95% confidence intervals. Unadjusted Fisher exact OR 10.02 (95% CI 3.13–36.66; P = 9.83e-06). Resistance at POP diagnosis is not a prospective predictor.

Table S6 — Sensitivity of candidate actionability

Table S6. Observed candidate proportion and extreme assumptions for unknown composite outcomes.
Scenario k N Estimate

Table S6 (PDF) · CSV

The composite is specific overlap plus inadequate empirical therapy. It is unknown in 2 patients; absence of overlap makes the composite negative even when adequacy is unavailable. Extreme scenarios bound the composite under the recorded microbiology, not the true clinical benefit. Result availability, susceptibility and coverage of the matching organism require chart adjudication.

The main definition requires at least one shared specific organism. More stringent definitions distinguish identical nonempty profiles from coverage of all documented specific POP organisms. Empty profiles never count as matches. These are species-level comparisons, not evidence of strain identity or antibiotic susceptibility.

Figure S4 — Concordance expected under random pairing

Figure S4. Distribution of specific concordance after 10,000 permutations of complete POP organism profiles among positive pre-EOT patients with known primary microbiology codes. The vertical line denotes observed concordance. Observed concordance was 33/81 (40.7%), compared with a mean of 4.9% under random pairing (one-sided Monte Carlo P = 1e-04). Exchangeability is assumed; shared surgery type, antibiotic exposure or calendar-period ecology may explain part of the association. This is exploratory and does not prove bacterial persistence.

Figure S5 — Temporal association with specific concordance

Figure S5. Estimated probability of specific overlap according to sampling-to-POP interval. Shading denotes pointwise 95% Wald confidence intervals; rug marks show observed intervals. The exploratory unadjusted logistic model estimated an OR per additional calendar day of 0.92 (95% CI 0.81–1.06; P = 0.25). The model assumes linearity on the log-odds scale; no optimal threshold or validated predictive performance is claimed.

Table S10 — Exploratory multivariable analysis

Table S10. Firth penalised logistic regression for empirical antimicrobial inadequacy; adjusted odds ratios and profile penalised likelihood 95% confidence intervals.
Covariate Adjusted OR 95% CI lower 95% CI upper P value
Reported resistance at POP diagnosis 9.330 3.320 29.40 1.41e-05
Antibiotics within 90 days before surgery 0.890 0.256 3.02 8.51e-01
Liver transplantation 0.974 0.291 3.21 9.65e-01

Table S10 (PDF) · CSV

The complete-case model included 100 patients and 22 inadequacy events. Covariates were selected on clinical grounds for this exploratory reanalysis: reported resistance, antibiotic exposure within 90 days before surgery and liver transplantation. The adjusted OR for resistance was 9.33 (95% CI 3.32–29.40). Penalisation reduces small-sample bias but does not eliminate imprecision, residual confounding or selection bias. Resistance at POP diagnosis is partly linked to the definition of adequacy; this is neither a causal model nor a prospective prediction model.

Clinical adjudication required before submission

The 8 observed candidate cases require review of microbiological result release time, susceptibility availability, whether the shared organism was uncovered by initial therapy, and whether a feasible alternative regimen would cover all relevant pathogens. These items cannot be inferred from sampling dates or species codes. Record them in a secure clinical workspace, not the public HTML. Report aggregate adjudication results only after verification.

Statistical interpretation and limitations

All additional analyses are exploratory and were developed after inspection of the original results. No multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory claims are made. This retrospective cohort contains only sampled patients who developed POP; it cannot estimate POP incidence, diagnostic performance for incident POP, or the causal benefit of routine sampling. The resistance association is unadjusted and partly reflects the definition of adequacy. A parsimonious exploratory Firth model is reported in Table S10; the small event count limits precision and adjustment for additional covariates. No post-hoc power calculation is used.
